provenanceNote: Finland and Sweden do not collide. Sweden's shapes are all digits with an optional '-' or '+' separator and a four-digit tail; a Finnish code's control character may be a letter, and this one is. detect() reports exactly one scheme. The near-miss is closer than it looks -- both write six date digits, a hyphen and four characters -- which is why the pair is worth asserting rather than assuming. Published by DVV on Suomi.fi for Service Developers and vendored at spec/sources/dvv/test-identities.csv. Individual number 952, inside the 900-999 block DVV states it does not issue from, so the code is entered in no population register and identifies nobody. CLAUDE.md's Exception 3.

The same DVV code with its intermediate character removed, which is what a caller 'normalising' a Finnish number by stripping separators would produce. It is not a Swedish number -- ten characters, but the last is a letter -- and it is no longer a Finnish one either, because decree 690/2022 makes the marker part of the identity rather than punctuation. detect() reports nothing at all. Constructed and invalid, so it needs no provenance exception: ten characters ending in a letter can have no bearer in any registry here. This is the fixture that would go red if anyone taught the normalizer to drop a Finnish marker the way it drops a Swedish one.
